learning_outcomes.text: Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess learning skills that allow continuous lifelong learning for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and industrial engineering technologies and tools into professional activities.
Know and apply knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge of the principles of theory of machines and mechanisms.
Ability to understand and interpret the results obtained from a kinematic and dynamic analysis of a mechanism.
Ability to determine positions, velocities, accelerations, and forces using analytical methods.
Ability to determine positions, velocities, accelerations, and forces using graphical methods.
Knowledge of the fundamental concepts and theorems in the theory of machines and mechanisms.
Knowledge and classification of basic mechanisms and their constituent parts.
Knowledge of the principles of theory of machines and mechanisms.
Proficiency in mechanism analysis and simulation software.

assessment_rules: For progressive assessment, the final grade is calculated as 0.6 * (global exam Block A) + 0.3 * (average of two partial tests) + 0.1 * (laboratory practices grade). If students voluntarily take Block B of the global exam, the better of two formulas is applied. A minimum grade of 5 points is required to pass, provided a minimum of 4 points in Block A and attendance to all 3 lab sessions are met; otherwise, the maximum possible grade is 4.8. For global ordinary assessment, the final grade is 0.6 * (global exam Block A) + 0.3 * (global exam Block B) + 0.1 * (laboratory practices grade), with the same passing conditions. For the extraordinary call, the final grade is the final exam score (100%), with a minimum of 5 points and attendance to all 3 lab sessions required to pass; otherwise, the maximum possible grade is 4.8.
